pk.context: 80 mg oral, single dose, healthy adults

tell: Only about 14% of the parent drug reaches the circulation, yet LDL-C lowering is the same with or without food.

clues.text: Absolute bioavailability of the parent drug is about 14%, and food changes absorption only modestly. It is at least 98% bound to plasma proteins and is cleared mainly by hepatic metabolism and biliary elimination.
A calcium salt trihydrate, crystalline and insoluble in aqueous solutions at pH 4 or below. The active moiety has a molecular weight of 558.6.
Approved under an NDA as tablets of 10, 20, 40 and 80 mg.
Contraindicated in acute liver failure, decompensated cirrhosis and hypersensitivity to the drug; no boxed warning. Myalgia and diarrhea are the commonest reactions leading to discontinuation.
Reducing heart attack, stroke, revascularization and angina in adults with coronary risk factors, and lowering LDL cholesterol in primary hyperlipidemia or familial hypercholesterolemia.
A selective, competitive inhibitor of HMG-CoA reductase, the enzyme that makes mevalonate, a cholesterol precursor. It raises liver LDL receptors, so more LDL is taken up and cleared.
The generic name begins with A and has twelve letters.
